questions.q: According to Hanh, what does love need in order to grow?
a: Nourishment in the form of happiness
Constant admiration from a partner
A shared home and daily routine
Freedom from every attachment
questions.why: Lesson 1 says love must be fed with happiness before it can expand and reach others.

questions.q: Which four qualities does the summary say love is made of?
a: Joy, equanimity, compassion and loving-kindness
Patience, honesty, loyalty and desire
Trust, passion, commitment and humor
Kindness, discipline, courage and wisdom
questions.why: Lesson 2 names joy, equanimity, compassion and loving-kindness as love's four traits.

questions.q: What does equanimity mean in the summary?
a: Blurring the line between their suffering and yours
Staying calm and detached when a partner is upset
Treating everyone with the same polite courtesy
Balancing work and love without feeling guilt
questions.why: Lesson 2 calls equanimity inclusiveness: another person's suffering becomes your own.

questions.q: How does Hanh suggest we treat the word love?
a: Reserve it for real love rather than for ice cream
Say it often so the people around us feel valued
Use it only when speaking to a romantic partner
Replace it with the Sanskrit word karuna
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the word loses value when used for things like ice cream, so use it mindfully.

questions.q: Why does the summary compare love to medicine?
a: It does more than understand pain, it helps heal it
It should be taken in small regular doses
It works best when prescribed by an expert
It can have side effects if given too freely
questions.why: Lesson 3 says love, like medicine, does not just recognize suffering but helps relieve it.
